spec.doc: StarTrack Label Specifications - Modify Your Own System (MOS) v9

rules.title: AI 00 SSCC freight barcode decoded
rules.description: SSCC retailer labels carry the article identifier as a GS1-128 barcode containing FNC1 + AI 00 + the 18-digit SSCC (20 digits including AI 00) and nothing else.

messages.pass: Valid AI 00 SSCC freight barcode(s) decoded.
messages.fail: SSCC assessment was selected, but no valid AI 00 SSCC freight barcode was decoded.

rules.title: SSCC check digit
rules.description: The final SSCC digit must satisfy the GS1 mod-10 check digit algorithm.

messages.pass: All decoded SSCC barcodes have valid mod-10 check digits.
messages.fail: One or more decoded SSCC values failed the mod-10 check digit.
messages.skipped: No SSCC barcode was decoded, so the check digit could not be assessed.

rules.title: GS1-128 FNC1 in first position
rules.description: A GS1-128 SSCC barcode starts with FNC1. Scanners report this as the code ]C1.

messages.pass: Scanner reported symbology identifier ]C1: FNC1 is encoded in the first position, so the symbol is a conforming GS1-128 SSCC barcode.
messages.fail: The reported symbology identifier indicates the symbol does NOT start with FNC1 - it decodes as plain Code 128, not GS1-128. See the identifier in the evidence.
messages.missing: The decoder did not report an ISO/IEC 15424 symbology identifier, so FNC1-in-first-position could not be verified digitally. Confirm the symbol was generated as GS1-128 (Code 128 with a leading FNC1), not plain Code 128.

rules.title: SSCC is in the merchant's range
rules.description: The SSCC must sit inside a StarTrack SSCC range from the merchant profile. Runs only when ranges are entered.

rules.title: SSCC uses a GS1 Australia prefix
rules.description: Australian merchants' SSCCs usually start with a GS1 Australia prefix (93). Another prefix is allowed, so this is a note. Skipped when the profile has SSCC ranges.
rules.expectedText: Starts with a GS1 Australia prefix (93)

messages.pass: SSCC {actual} uses a GS1 Australia company prefix.
messages.fail: SSCC {actual} doesn't use a GS1 Australia prefix (93). That's allowed, but confirm it's the merchant's registered prefix.

rules.title: SSCC labels are despatch movements only
rules.description: SSCC barcodes may only be used for despatch movements, never for controlled returns or transfers.

messages.pass: QR movement type is N (despatch), as required for SSCC labels.
messages.fail: QR movement type is {actual}. SSCC barcodes may only be used for despatch movements.
messages.empty: No StarTrack QR barcode was read, so the despatch-only rule couldn't be checked. SSCC barcodes are for despatch only, so check the label isn't a return or transfer.

rules.title: Human-readable SSCC digits match the barcode
rules.description: The 20 human-readable SSCC digits printed with the AI 00 symbol must equal the decoded SSCC. Compared against print-only text so the barcode cannot vouch for itself.

messages.pass: Printed SSCC digits match the decoded AI 00 SSCC.
messages.fail: The printed SSCC digits do not match the decoded AI 00 SSCC ({actual}). Check it on the label. Overlays and watermarks can throw off text reading.
messages.skipped: No printed SSCC digits were read, so they couldn't be compared with the barcode.

rules.title: Product comes from QR
rules.description: SSCC numbers can't carry a StarTrack product, so the product comes from the QR and routing barcodes.

messages.pass: SSCC labels don't carry a product, so it comes from the QR and routing barcodes.
